entities.summary:
Archias of Thurii in Magna Graecia was an actor turned military agent of the Macedonian general Antipater in the 4th century BCE. He was nicknamed “thunter of the exiles’ (_phygaidothēras). This remarkable individual played a pivotal role in the Hellenistic period, as Antipater sought to reassert Macedonian control in the Greek city-states. Archias’ exceptional skills and strategic prowess allowed him to outmaneuver his opponents, earning him a reputation as a cunning and ruthless operative. His exploits have been chronicled by the historian Polyaenus, who credited him with facilitating the capture of the city of Agrigentum. 

Archias was born in Thurii, a city in southern Italy, and died under unknown circumstances. His legacy has been studied by scholars of ancient Greek history, who note that he was a key figure in the tumultuous period following the death of Alexander the Great.

Archias’ military campaigns were marked by his ability to infiltrate enemy cities and gather intelligence, often using his acting skills to gain the trust of his targets. He was particularly effective in his role as a ‘thunter of exiles’, using his charisma and cunning to persuade people to defect from their homes and join the Macedonian army.

Despite his formidable reputation, Archias’ personal life remains shrouded in mystery. His exact date of birth and death are unknown, and scholars have long debated the accuracy of Polyaenus’ accounts of his exploits. Nevertheless, Archias remains an intriguing figure in the history of ancient Greece, whose name has been invoked by historians and scholars for centuries.
